repository.note: The repository this agent reviews pull requests in. This file lives IN that repository (typically .github/copilot/agents/reviewer.config.json), and its location is also what tells the agent where the repository root is.
repository.name: Example-Service

customAgent.note: Empty name = no Agency custom agent. review-cycle.prompt.md IS the complete instruction set; loading an unrelated repo agent (for example a squad coordinator) on top of it makes the model adopt that persona and never emit a result marker.

operator.note: Default alias the agent runs AS. Its own pull requests are excluded from review. The -OperatorAlias wrapper parameter is authoritative and overrides this. Leave empty in a checked-in config so the repository does not name an individual.

review.note: targetRefName scopes the agent to pull requests aimed at the mainline. maxFindings is the per-PR posting cap; the model is told the same number so it self-prioritizes instead of being truncated. postSeverities is what this repository is willing to have posted - findings at other severities are still reported in the preview file and counted in the summary.

threadClassification.note: Identities whose comments are NOT human review feedback. Used to build the metadata digest the model sees, so that a bot's or a policy service's output is not mistaken for a reviewer's opinion.

teamsNotifications.note: Checked-in config alone NEVER delivers anything: the operator must also pass -EnableTeamsNotifications, and startup fails if that switch is passed while nothing here is enabled - so the switch can never silently do nothing. Webhook URLs and secrets are never stored here.

workIq.note: Verified WorkIQ contract: 'fetch' takes an entityUrls ARRAY, 'create_entity' takes parentUrl + jsonBody, and the payload returns in structuredContent (NOT content[]). A non-2xx statusCode is a failure even when the MCP call itself succeeds.

directAuthor.note: One-on-one Teams chat. Microsoft Graph cannot create a chat between the signed-in user and themselves, so recipientUpn must be a DIFFERENT person than whoever the agent runs as. Independent of the channel destination - either alone is valid.

repoConventions.note: Injected into the agent's runtime context as DATA. Keeps repository-specific engineering rules OUT of the shared prompt, so the prompt - and the result-marker contract it defines - stays identical for every consumer.
repoConventions.customRules: Public API changes require a corresponding entry in docs/api-changes.md. Prefer flagging a missing test over speculating about runtime behaviour the diff does not show.

permissions.note: The wrapper's code-defined ceiling is read-only and this list may only NARROW it. Write tools - including ado(repo_pull_request_thread_write) and ado(repo_pull_request_write) - are mandatory denies that no config can grant: the model reports findings as structured data and the WRAPPER performs every write. Two whole families are rejected outright no matter what is listed here. shell(...) is rejected even for commands that look read-only, because `git diff --output=<path>` and `git log --output=<path>` write files, so no argument-prefix grant on a shell command is safe. web_search and web_fetch are rejected because this agent reads private source and private review threads, and an outbound request whose URL the model composes is an exfiltration channel.
